Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! The umpires are strolling to their positions and the Pakistan Under-19 players are scattered to take their positions for fielding. Amir Hassan is with the new ball to start the bowling attack. Wafiullah Tarakhil and Hassan Eisakhil to open for Afghanistan Under-19. Here we go...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

On the other hand, Afghanistan's bowling unit was decent enough at the initial stages, but they were a bit expensive as the game started flowing. Their opening bowlers were putting a bit of pressure on the opposition openers but they weren't able to get the breakthroughs. All thanks to Khalil Ahmed, who drew the first two bloods for his team their opponent. But after that, they iced the situation and also spilled three catches, which would help them dismiss Shahzaib Khan much earlier in the innings which they rued for the rest of the innings. But huge credit to the skipper, who brought Allah Mohammad into the attack and broke the well-shaped partnership between Khan and Saad Baig. Naseer Khan Maroofkhil also chipped in for a wicket. Now all pressure is on the batters and it would be interesting to see how Afghanistan Under-19 will plan to turn the ship of the game towards their side. Join us in a bit for the chase.

Saad Baig, the skipper of Pakistan Under-19 is up for a chat. He says it was tough to bat in the pitch at the initial stage of the inning. He continues that when he was at the pitch to start his innings he discussed with Shahzaib Khan that they should take time and have a good score on the board. He also praises Khan for his incredible knock and says that Shahzaib Khan was confident enough to perform well. He ends up saying that he and his bowlers are positive enough to defend the massive total and win the match for the nation.

Pakistan Under-19 did their job perfectly after opting to bat first. Their openers started things calmly and steadily. After the 10th over they lost two wickets in quick succession but the skipper, Saad Baig anchored the situation and formed a hefty partnership with the other opener, Shahzaib Khan. Khan got three lifelines as a gift from the Afghans and he capitalized on it pretty much throughout his innings. They formed a partnership of 92 runs where Saad Baig played a knock of 55 runs but got dismissed in the 28th over. After the fall of the fourth wicket, Shahzaib and Riaz Ullah steadied things and constructed a firm partnership of 84 runs. Shahzaib Khan kept on batting well despite losing partners at the other end, crafted an extraordinary inning, and became the 8th Pakistani batter to score a century at this level, and ended up scoring 106 runs off 125 deliveries. Ubaid Shah also played a handy little cameo towards the end. It looks like there are enough runs on the board for their bowlers to defend, but we know that anything can happen in cricket.

Take a bow, Shahzaib Khan! What an incredible ton it was from him! He was out there in the middle as an opener and played till the end of the innings. Pakistan Under-19 have challenged Afghanistan Under-19 posting a total of 284 runs. The Afghans will need to break the record of the highest successful chase at this level to get the win here.

We are moments away from the start of the game but before that, the players from both sides line up for their respective national anthems. It will be Afghanistan's first followed by the national anthem of Pakistan.

PITCH REPORT - Marina Iqbal is pitchside. She says that it is a neutral pitch. Adds that it is a bit dry with patches of grass on it. Tells that there are a few cracks on it which indicates that there will be variable bounce. Says that the pacers will get help, but the batters will also enjoy batting on this surface.

Naseer Khan Maroofkhil, the captain of Afghanistan Under-19 says that the wicket is looking fresh and they anyway wanted to bowl first. He continues that they have played a couple of series against South Africa and India so they have spent a lot of time in the country which will certainly help. He ends up saying they are just going to follow the coach's order and try their level best to win the game.

Saad Baig, the skipper of Pakistan Under-19 says that they will bat first. Adds that they want to score big and defend it. He continues that they have played against Afghanistan Under-19 before also but it's advantageous for both teams as they are aware of the the strengths and weaknesses of each other. He ends up saying that he believes in his players and he is confident that the match will go in their.favour.

On the other hand, Pakistan boasts a strong record of dominance against Afghanistan in head-to-head encounters. Drawing confidence from recent triumphs over Afghanistan and Team India in December, their top-order batters exhibit resilience which they showed in previous matches as well. Their bowling unit is also pretty good and strong with Ubaid Shah leading the pack with his ability to swing the ball both ways on command. Will the Men in Green once again outclass their opponents? Or can the Afghans secure their first victory against Pakistan since September 2019? Let's find out! Toss and team news in a bit.

Afghanistan's recent performances have been subpar, but they faced top teams like India and South Africa in a tri-nation tournament. Even though the results did not go in their way, the experience would have surely helped them to prepare for this big event. They should take the positives from that series and rectify the mistakes to put up a challenge for the opponents. Their batting lineup is holds promise, but consistency will be key for a successful outcome. Allah Mohammad stands out as the sole bowler who has been able to pick up wickets in all of the recent matches, and the skipper, Numan Shah will have huge expectations from him to lead the bowling front for the team.
